    🏔 Meteorologist Forecast
    Temira, The Gorge Is My Gym · posted Fri Nov 13 · full post ↗

    Hey skiers and snowboarders! It’s Friday! Snow levels fluctuate between too-high and low-enough through Sunday morning, after which they’ll be below 5000′ for several days. We’ll pick up under a foot of snow in that period; the most likely scenario is about 5”. Starting next Friday, temps will probably rise again and take the snow level back above 5000′ for the extended period, through the 27thof November. Just a heads up: I’m taking off on a meditation retreat on Sunday, so there will be a pause in the forecast until Tuesday, 11/24.

    Let’s look at Friday, shall we? The snow level will be 7500′ in the morning, 6000′ in the afternoon, and 5000′ after midnight. About a quarter inch of rain falls during the day. Overnight, we pick up just 0.1” water equivalent (WE) for an inch of snow at 5000′. Wind will be S 20-40 this morning, S 10-20 this afternoon, and SW 20-40 after midnight.

    Saturday starts with snow, but rising temps switch us over to mixed precip then rain. The snow level climbs from 5000′ in the morning to 8000′ in the evening and falls to 6500′ after midnight. Up to have an inch of moisture falls in that time period, mostly as rain. Wind: SW 15-20 much of the day rising to SW 30-50 after midnight.

    Rain Sunday morning transitions to snow midday. The sky clears in the afternoon. Snow level: 6500′ early, 5000′ in the afternoon, and 3000′ under mostly clear sky overnight. Just a quarter inch of precip is forecast in that period for maybe an inch of snow at 5000′. Wind: SW 30-50 early becoming WSW 15 in the afternoon and W 10-15 overnight.

    Looking at the extended forecast: flurries are likely on Monday. Dry weather returns Tuesday. During that time period, the freezing level should be under 5000′. A wetter system early Wednesday brings a few inches of snow with temps at 5000′ in the 28-30F range. Thursday looks dry and cool. Beyond that, uncertainty is present, but it’s likely temps will be too warm for snow at 5000′ through the 27th. That’s all for now. Keep practicing patience, and by patience, I mean dryland training! See you on the snow soon!
